violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: milk at 47F, corn salsa at 47F stored in #9 2 DR UC Cabinet Left Expo; scrambled egg mixture at 50F on cold rail on cook line; corn salsa at 53F, shredded American cheese at 58F on ice near soup warmers; avocado cream at 50F, pico de gallo at 50F in #17 6 DWR/Cold rail; cooked chicken at 46F in #20 2 DWR; kimchi at 50F in #22 6 DWR/cold rail.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. CFM agreed to discard at 1500:milk, corn salsa, scrambled egg, corn salsa, shredded American cheese, cooked chicken. Ice was placed on top of avocado cream, pico de gallo. Kimchi moved to unit able to maintain 41F or below. EHS and CFM discussed using TPHC for corn salsa and shredded cheese used for soup garnish. CFM noted items in violation were overfilled in container. CFM discussed with employees correct fill line portion for containers. CFM will discuss with head chef rearranging items on cold rail at #22, since placement of some TCS foods - kimchi- are directly under salamander.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: observed large batches of cooked pasta with lid on container in #11.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. CFM had employee remove lid and move pastas to WIF to facilitate faster cooling.

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: various squirt bottles with oils and sauces on cookline.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. CFM had employee label bottles with food name. CHEESECAKE FACTORY (Inspection Date: 07/15/2025) Page 3 of 4
